title: Amazon is cutting nearly 1,000 jobs in its retail division
source_used: Fox Business, relaying Reuters and Business Insider
key_facts: Amazon is cutting fewer than 1,000 white-collar jobs, mainly in its stores division, according to Reuters.
Business Insider was first to report the cuts.
Internal Slack messages reviewed by Reuters suggest several divisions are affected, including customer service and selling partner services.
Employees in the US, India and the UK are reportedly among those hit.
An Amazon spokesperson said it was eliminating a small number of roles to better deliver on its priorities.
The cuts follow about 30,000 corporate job cuts that began last year and continued into January.
quote_evidence: Amazon is cutting fewer than 1,000 white-collar jobs, mainly in its stores division, which oversees the company's main e-commerce website, according to Reuters.
Business Insider was the first to report the latest layoffs.
why_it_matters_hint: A further, smaller round of cuts at Amazon after about 30,000 earlier corporate cuts.
notes: Quartz page blocked (403); read the Fox Business article, which relays Reuters and Business Insider. Quartz and other headlines say nearly 1,000; Fox/Reuters say fewer than 1,000. No AI link is stated in the text read.
